name: Denmark
sub: The national harmonised 10-fraction system with shared pictograms used by every municipality.

banana.w: Food scraps go in the green food-waste bin and become biogas and fertiliser.

eggshell.w: Egg shells are listed as food waste alongside other kitchen scraps.

coffee.w: Coffee grounds and paper filters both go in food waste.

bones.w: Bones and fish bones are accepted in Danish food waste.

shampoo.w: Empty plastic bottles go in plastic; the cap can stay on.

polybag.w: Soft plastic like carrier bags is collected with hard plastic in Denmark.

chips.w: Most kommuner say residual because it is mixed foil; if it carries the plastic pictogram, plastic is fine.

tube.w: Copenhagen says plastic or metal by material; some kommuner, like Aarhus, want tubes in residual.

carton.w: Milk cartons have their own fraction; empty them, no rinsing needed.

eggtray.w: Clean egg trays usually go with cardboard, but a few kommuner send them to residual.

box.w: Flatten cardboard boxes and put them in the cardboard (pap) bin.

pizza.w: Food residue spoils the cardboard, so it is residual; Copenhagen now accepts empty pizza boxes as cardboard.

newspaper.w: Newspapers are the classic paper fraction and get recycled into new paper.

jar.w: Empty glass jars go in glass; put metal lids in metal.

wine.w: Wine bottles have no deposit in Denmark, so they go in the glass bin.

perfume.w: An empty perfume bottle can go in glass; remove the pump and cap if possible.

tin.w: Empty food tins go in metal; no need to wash them.

window.w: Small shards of window glass can go in residual, wrapped; whole panes go to the genbrugsplads.

drinkglass.w: Unlike many countries, Danish glass collection takes drinking glasses and wrapped shards too.

mirror.w: Mirror glass has a coating that spoils glass recycling, so small pieces go in residual.

tissue.w: Used tissues are residual waste in Denmark, not food waste.

diaper.w: Nappies are residual waste and are burned for district heating.

pad.w: Hygiene products go in residual waste.

battery.w: Batteries are hazardous; use the kommune's battery bag or box, or a shop collection point.

bulb.w: Energy-saving bulbs contain mercury, so take them to hazardous waste or the genbrugsplads.

meds.w: Leftover medicine is hazardous waste; hand it in at any pharmacy (apotek).

paint.w: Paint with contents left is hazardous waste; take it to the genbrugsplads or miljøkasse.

toy.w: Plastic toys without electronics can go in plastic; larger ones go to the genbrugsplads.
